'''David P. Madson'''<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.xlr8r.com/mp3/2009/02/fly-mode/|title=Odd Nosdam "Fly Mode"|work=XLR8R|first=Jennifer|last=Marston|date=February 24, 2009}}</ref> (born 1976),<ref name=allmusic/> better known by his stage name '''Odd Nosdam''', is an American [[underground hip hop]] [[hip hop production|producer]], [[disc jockey|DJ]] and visual artist.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.xlr8r.com/mp3/2008/04/forever-heavy-shoegangster-jb-remix/|title=Odd Nosdam "Forever Heavy (Shoegangster/JB Remix)"|work=XLR8R|first=Bryant|last=Rutledge|date=April 23, 2008}}</ref> He is co-founder of the record label [[Anticon]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tinymixtapes.com/news/odd-nosdam-announces-the-digital-release-of-t-r-i-s-h-a-musical-tribute-to-broadcasts-trish-kee|title=Odd Nosdam announces the digital release of T R I S H, a musical tribute to Broadcast's Trish Keenan|work=Tiny Mix Tapes|first=Mike|last=Reid|date=September 18, 2013}}</ref> He has remixed tracks by a variety of bands and artists including [[Boards of Canada]], [[The Notwist]], and [[Sole (hip hop artist)|Sole]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soundcolourvibration.com/2011/11/11/odd-nosdam-interview/|title=Anticon's Odd Nosdam gives Sound Colour Vibration an exclusive interview|first=Erik|last=Otis|work=Sound Colour Vibration |date=November 11, 2011}}</ref>

==History==
Odd Nosdam was first noticed for his production on ''[[Clouddead (album)|cLOUDDEAD]]'', the debut album released in 2001 by [[Clouddead|cLOUDDEAD]], his former group with [[Yoni Wolf]] of [[Why? (American band)|Why?]] and [[Doseone]].<ref name=allmusic>{{cite web|url=http://www.allmusic.com/artist/odd-nosdam-mn0000468695/biography|title=Biography: Odd Nosdam|last=Brown|first=Marisa|website=[[Allmusic]]|access-date=9 June 2010}}</ref> In 2002, under the name [[Reaching Quiet]], [[Yoni Wolf]] and Nosdam released their collaborative effort, ''[[In the Shadow of the Living Room]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dustedmagazine.com/reviews/248|title=Reaching Quiet - in the shadow of the livingroom|publisher=Dusted Magazine|first=Daniel|last=Thomas-Glass|date=June 25, 2002}}</ref> Nosdam's third beat tape, ''[[No More Wig for Ohio]]'', self-released in 2002, was rereleased by [[Anticon]] in 2003.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dustedmagazine.com/reviews/729|title=Odd Nosdam - No More Wig For Ohio|publisher=Dusted Magazine|first=Brian|last=Ho|date=May 15, 2003}}</ref>

In 2005, Odd Nosdam released his first proper solo album, ''[[Burner (Odd Nosdam album)|Burner]]'', which features [[Örvar Þóreyjarson Smárason]] of [[múm]], [[Jessica Bailiff]], Andrew Broder of [[Fog (band)|Fog]], [[Dosh (musician)|Dosh]], and [[Dax Pierson]], among others.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dustedmagazine.com/reviews/2256|title=Odd Nosdam - Burner|publisher=Dusted Magazine|first=Charlie|last=Wilmoth|date=July 1, 2005}}</ref> ''[[Level Live Wires]]'', Nosdam's second solo album, was released in 2007 and features [[Tunde Adebimpe]] of [[TV on the Radio]], Dee Kesler of [[Thee More Shallows]], Chris Adams of [[Hood (band)|Hood]], [[Jel (rapper)|Jel]], and [[Jessica Bailiff]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/10977-level-live-wires/|title=Odd Nosdam: Level Live Wires|publisher=Pitchfork Media|first=Joshua|last=Love|date=January 18, 2008}}</ref> Also in 2007, Nosdam created the soundtrack for [[Element Skateboards]] video ''[[This Is My Element]]'' and in 2009, released the music as the ''[[T.I.M.E. Soundtrack]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.xlr8r.com/reviews/odd-nosdam/t-i-m-e-soundtrack|title=T.I.M.E. Soundtrack|publisher=XLR8R|first=Chris|last=Sabbath|date=February 27, 2009}}</ref>

[[Serengeti (rapper)|Serengeti]], Jel, and Odd Nosdam's first collaborative effort, ''[[Kenny Dennis EP]]'', was released in 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/16436-serengeti-kenny-dennis-ep/|title=Serengeti - Kenny Dennis EP|website=Pitchfork|first=Jeff|last=Weiss|date=March 27, 2012}}</ref> It was followed by ''[[C.A.R. (album)|C.A.R.]]'',<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chicagoreader.com/chicago/hannibal-buress-kyle-kinane-rockie-fresh-jel-serengeti-dj-tony-trimm/Event?oid=6879903|title=Hannibal Buress, Kyle Kinane, Rockie Fresh, Jel, Serengeti, DJ Tony Trimm|work=Chicago Reader|first=Leor|last=Galil|date=July 13, 2012}}</ref> ''[[Kenny Dennis LP]]'',<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.latimes.com/entertainment/music/posts/la-et-ms-in-rotation-20130630-story.html|title=In Rotation: 'Avalanche' by Quadron, 'Kenny Dennis LP' by Serengeti|work=Los Angeles Times|first=Randall|last=Roberts|date=June 29, 2013}}</ref> ''C.A.B.'',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.spin.com/2013/12/serengeti-doseone-sprung-cab-jel-nosdam-stream/|title=Hear Serengeti and Doseone's Bluesy Rap Bruiser 'Sprung'|work=Spin|first=Chris|last=Martins|date=December 11, 2013}}</ref> and ''[[Kenny Dennis III]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/19941-serengeti-kenny-dennis-iii/|title=Serengeti: Kenny Dennis III|work=Pitchfork Media|first=Nate|last=Patrin|date=November 21, 2014}}</ref>
